tasks.short: Inspect sporting equipment and participants for rule compliance

steps.what: Inspect sporting equipment and examine participants against applicable event and safety regulations

tasks.design: Retain physical inspection and rule application with the official, using the event rules in {DOCS}. A checklist may support consistency but does not replace inspection of the actual person or equipment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Compliance depends on actual condition and context rather than a previously stored identifier.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest does not demonstrate replacement of this physical event-safety inspection.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising hidden damage, unsuitable equipment and circumstances that require stopping participation.
tasks.human_edge: The official can inspect the current situation and ask for correction or clarification immediately.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in inspection responsibility or event-safety decision rights.

reach.task: Explain a concrete equipment or venue concern
reach.learn: Event rule applicability and correction routes

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: physical sports equipment and participant checks remain human; no task-specific labour saving is demonstrated by the digest.

assumptions: Boundary is the official's inspection and immediate findings, excluding equipment repair, medical examination by another professional and later disciplinary reporting.

The official identifies event, rule version, equipment or participant, observed condition and required correction during s1. Capture and checking are fully counted; no structured safe, eligible or compliant flag is assumed.
Uncertain condition or rule applicability requires manual reinspection or referral to the responsible event authority, not inferred clearance.
Use existing native references and checklists. No new system or process is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
research_questions: Is there separately measurable duplicate inspection recording beyond the essential physical check?

already_counted.description: Inspect actual conditions and apply the event rules

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives gross0 and net0 with zero upkeep. Routine equipment checks and an uncertain participant restriction retain full inspection and judgement time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Report sporting complaints and actions to regulating organisations

steps.what: Establish the sporting activity, complaint facts, actions taken and any recommendation needing report
outputs: checked report facts and official recommendation

steps.what: Populate the required report form with the checked event facts and supporting references
inputs: checked report facts and official recommendation

steps.what: Check the report's meaning, distinguish facts from recommendations and submit it to the regulating organisation
inputs: checked report facts and official recommendation
outputs: submitted sporting activity or disciplinary report

tasks.design: Configure the existing reporting template in {DOCS} to reuse checked factual fields and the official's own recommendation. The official verifies the final wording and submits through the sports organisation portal in {OTHER}; no fine or disciplinary outcome is generated or imposed automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same event and incident facts may be copied into a formal report.
tasks.enabler_now: Native forms can place explicit facts without interpreting misconduct or deciding sanctions.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing direct observation, allegations, actions already taken and recommendations for others to decide.
tasks.human_edge: The official can judge whether the report fairly represents what occurred and what remains uncertain.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated form preparation; accountability for the report and disciplinary decision boundaries stay unchanged.

reach.task: Provide a clear account separating observation and recommendation

evidence.claim: The KNVB Wedstrijdzaken app supports a digital match form and referee-entered results; this is evidence of sports reporting software, not automated disciplinary judgement.
Model knowledge: a fixed report template can reuse checked incident fields; the proposed complaint-report saving is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is report preparation and submission by the official, excluding the live incident decision and the regulating organisation's investigation or sanction decision.

In s1 the official produces event and participant references, incident time, factual description, complaint attribution, action already taken, recommendation, uncertainty and evidence references. All fact capture, interpretation and correction remain fully counted.

OTHER means the sports organisation reporting portal. The reporting owner supplies required fields and template versions, with added upkeep charged below. The machine only copies supplied facts and verbatim recommendations; it does not infer a discrepancy code, offence or sanction.

Test native forms first. Missing identities, disputed facts or unsupported attachments use manual report preparation and verification in s3. Any report shared with another reporting task must be assigned once in a roll-up.
unknowns: Sport-specific reporting forms and sanction authority
Whether the existing portal already reuses these facts
research_questions: Can native form reuse remove copying without blurring allegations, observed facts and sanction recommendations?

already_counted.description: Establish report facts and recommendations and check and submit the report

incremental.description: Handle form exceptions and verify reporting-template changes
Maintain required report fields and template versions

approvals.approved_version: Exact report snapshot, observed facts, complaint attribution, actions, recommendation, attachments and recipient; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R75 gives gross25, less focal upkeep7 gives net18. Range0-4 assumes many reports already use native fields and only occasional repeated copying is removed; fact assessment and final verification retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer with officials, participants and facility managers

steps.what: Confer with officials, coaches, players and facility managers to coordinate activities and discuss problems

tasks.design: Keep the live coordination conversation with the official and the relevant people. Existing event references in {DOCS} may inform discussion, but no separate briefing or scheduling-paperwork baseline is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coordination depends on changing circumstances and agreement among the people involved.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest does not demonstrate removal of this substantive conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Handling disagreement and making sure everyone understands the agreed action.
tasks.human_edge: The official can recognise confusion and adapt the discussion to the people and current event.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in coordination responsibility or time.

reach.task: Clarify an event arrangement or unresolved facility issue
reach.learn: Clear handoffs and event escalation routes

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: live sporting-event coordination and problem discussion remain human; no labour saving is established by the supplied digest.

assumptions: Boundary is the official's discussion, excluding other participants' time and any subsequent action or separate report.

The official establishes the issue, affected people, actual constraints and agreed next action during s1. Capture and clarification remain fully counted; no structured agreement or facility-ready flag is assumed.
Other people supply their questions and current circumstances in the conversation. Missing information or disagreement requires direct clarification.
Use existing native event references. No new process or integration is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether any distinct repetitive coordination administration exists
research_questions: Can a discussion sample identify repeat administration without reducing clarification and agreement time?

already_counted.description: Share information, discuss problems and agree coordination

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives gross0 and net0 with zero upkeep. Routine coordination and a disputed event problem both retain full discussion and clarification time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Judge sports performances and determine points and penalties

steps.what: Judge sporting performances, award points and apply scoring penalties under the competition rules

tasks.design: Keep performance judgement and application of penalties with the authorised official, using the rules in {DOCS}. Sport-specific review support may inform an inquiry, but this proposal claims no replacement of observation or judging time.
tasks.previous_blocker: A scoring decision depends on the observed performance and the competition's interpretation rules.
tasks.enabler_now: A documented judging-support case is limited to inquiries or blocked scores, rather than universal autonomous judging.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting marginal performances and applying penalties consistently under time pressure.
tasks.human_edge: The official can weigh the permitted evidence in the context of the actual performance.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in judging authority or observation time.

reach.task: Explain the awarded points and penalties clearly

evidence.claim: At the 2023 Antwerp gymnastics championships, the FIG and Fujitsu Judging Support System was used on inquiries or blocked scores; the digest gives no counted use volume or labour saving.

assumptions: Boundary is performance observation and judging, excluding separate score compilation, arithmetic verification and report preparation. Those tasks must not be counted again here.

The official produces the performance assessment, event or attempt reference, awarded components, observed infringement and penalty decision during s1. Capture and judgement remain fully counted; no pre-existing structured performance or infringement flag is assumed.
Permitted review evidence comes from the existing event review process and is checked by the official. Unclear evidence follows the sport's manual inquiry procedure.
Use existing native scoring and review arrangements. No new model or integration is proposed, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Sport, scoring rules and permitted review procedures
research_questions: Is there any separately measurable score arithmetic beyond the performance judgement itself?

already_counted.description: Observe performance and determine points and penalties

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives gross0 and net0 with zero upkeep. An uncontroversial performance and a marginal scoring inquiry both retain full judging time; no inquiry-system accuracy is converted into labour saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repeated report form entry where present while protecting physical inspection, live coordination and performance judgement.
reach: Provide regulating officers with clearly attributed facts
Give event managers precise coordination and equipment concerns
role.ambitious_version: A sports official who spends less time copying settled report facts and retains the attention needed for fair judging and clear event communication.
